```{r gbk to fasta}
# Conversion from GenBank to nucleotide FASTA, as this is the input format required by QUAST, CheckM2 and mlplasmids. 


carpetaGBK   <- "Datos/genomas/GENBANK"
carpetaFASTA <- "Datos/genomas/FASTA"
dir.create(carpetaFASTA, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

archivosGBK <- list.files(carpetaGBK, pattern = "\\.gbk$", full.names = TRUE)

for (archivo in archivosGBK) {

  lineas <- readLines(archivo, warn = FALSE)

  ini_locus <- grep("^LOCUS",  lineas)
  ini_seq   <- grep("^ORIGIN", lineas)
  fin_seq   <- grep("^//",     lineas)

  nombres <- sub("^LOCUS\\s+(\\S+).*", "\\1", lineas[ini_locus])

  resultado <- character(2 * length(nombres))

  for (i in seq_along(nombres)) {
    bloque <- lineas[(ini_seq[i] + 1):(fin_seq[i] - 1)]
#Numbers and spaces are removed, while retaining N and IUPAC ambiguity codes.

    resultado[2 * i - 1] <- paste0(">", nombres[i])
    resultado[2 * i]     <- paste(gsub("[^A-Za-z]", "", bloque), collapse = "")
  }

  writeLines(resultado, file.path(carpetaFASTA,
                                  gsub("\\.gbk$", ".fasta", basename(archivo))))
}

cat("Generated FASTA files:", length(list.files(carpetaFASTA, pattern = "\\.fasta$")), "\n")
```

## 0. Quality control and other parameters
Before starting the analysis, the quality of the 30 initial genomic assemblies was assessed. These corresponded to antibiotic-resistant E. coli strains isolated at Uppsala University Hospital (Sweden) between 2014 and 2015, received already assembled and annotated in GenBank format.

Quality control was performed in Galaxy using two complementary tools: QUAST, which assesses assembly size and contiguity, and CheckM2, which estimates genome completeness and contamination based on single-copy marker genes.

Based on these results, 2 of the 30 strains were excluded due to anomalous contamination and/or assembly fragmentation: DA63738 (6.53% contamination and atypical %GC) and DA64006 (highly fragmented assembly with 25 contigs). Thus, 28 strains were retained for the subsequent analyses.

For the 28 retained strains, 4 samples showed discrepancies in the number of contigs reported by QUAST and CheckM2. This is expected because QUAST excludes contigs shorter than 500 bp, whereas CheckM2 does not apply this length filter. Therefore, the discrepancy does not indicate an error in either tool.

```{r QC data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
carpeta_quast <- "Resultados/qc/quast"
archivos_quast <- list.files(carpeta_quast, pattern = "\\.tabular$", full.names = TRUE)


leer_quast <- function(f) {
  read_tsv(f, col_names = c("metrica", "valor"), col_types = "cc") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = metrica, values_from = valor)
}

quast_raw <- map_dfr(archivos_quast, leer_quast) |>
  clean_names()

cat("Samples read from QUAST:", nrow(quast_raw), "\n")

quast_final <- quast_raw |>
  mutate(muestra = str_extract(assembly, "^[^_]+"), .before = 1) |>
  select(muestra, number_contigs, total_length, largest_contig, gc_percent, n50, n90, l50, l90) |>
  mutate(across(-muestra, as.numeric)) |>
  rename_with(~ paste0(., "_quast"), -muestra)

checkm2_final <- read_tsv("Resultados/qc/checkm2.tabular") |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(muestra = str_extract(name, "^[^_]+"), .before = 1) |>
  select(muestra, completeness_general, contamination, genome_size, gc_content,
         total_coding_sequences, total_contigs, max_contig_length, contig_n50) |>
  rename_with(~ paste0(., "_checkm2"), -muestra)
cat("Samples read from CheckM2:", nrow(checkm2_final), "\n")
qc_completo <- quast_final |>
  full_join(checkm2_final, by = "muestra")

muestras_excluidas <- c("DA63738", "DA64006")

qc_completo <- qc_completo |>
  mutate(excluida = muestra %in% muestras_excluidas)

qc_final_28 <- qc_completo |>
  filter(!excluida)

discrepancias_contigs <- qc_final_28 |>
  filter(number_contigs_quast != total_contigs_checkm2) |>
  select(muestra, number_contigs_quast, total_contigs_checkm2) |>
  mutate(diferencia = total_contigs_checkm2 - number_contigs_quast)

knitr::kable(
  discrepancias_contigs,
  caption = "Samples with discrepancies in the number of contigs between QUAST and CheckM2",
  col.names = c(
    "Sample",
    "No. of contigs (QUAST)",
    "No. of contigs (CheckM2)",
    "Difference"
  )
)
```

```{r QC plot, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
orden_muestras_qc <- plot_qc |> dplyr::arrange(desc(contamination_checkm2)) |> dplyr::pull(muestra)
```

To determine the replicon type (chromosome or plasmid) of each contig, mlplasmids was used, a machine-learning-based classifier specifically trained for different bacterial species, including *E. coli*. Based on sequence features of each contig, mlplasmids provides the probability of belonging to the chromosome (Prob_Chromosome) or plasmid (Prob_Plasmid), together with the resulting final prediction (Prediction). A total of 136 contigs were obtained, 84 of which were classified as plasmids and 52 as chromosomes.

```{r mlplasmids, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

library(mlplasmids, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

carpetaFASTA  <- "Datos/genomas/FASTA"
archivosFASTA <- list.files(carpetaFASTA, pattern = "\\.fasta$", full.names = TRUE)

lista_resultados <- lapply(archivosFASTA, function(archivo) {
  res <- plasmid_classification(
    path_input_file = archivo,
    species         = "Escherichia coli",
    prob_threshold  = 0.5, 
    min_length      = 500, 
    full_output     = TRUE
  )
  res$sample_name <- basename(archivo)
  res
})

tabla_plasmidos <- bind_rows(lista_resultados)
dir.create("Resultados/replicon/mlplasmid", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv2(tabla_plasmidos, "Resultados/replicon/mlplasmid/resultados_replicon.csv",
           row.names = FALSE)

mlplasmids_final <- read_csv2("Resultados/replicon/mlplasmid/resultados_replicon.csv") |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(muestra = str_extract(sample_name, "^[^_]+"), .before = 1) |>
  filter(!muestra %in% muestras_excluidas)

knitr::kable(
  tibble(
    Type = c("Plasmids", "Chromosomes", "Total contigs"),
    `Nº contigs` = c(
      sum(mlplasmids_final$prediction == "Plasmid"),
      sum(mlplasmids_final$prediction == "Chromosome"),
      nrow(mlplasmids_final)
    )
  )
)
```

## 1. Extraction of CDSs, transposases, and neighboring regions
All transposases were extracted from the .GBK files. A gene was considered a transposase if its functional product annotation contained the word "transposase". We identified 2,461 transposase annotations, reduced to 2,342 after the frameshift correction described below.
 
```{r Extraction of transposases , cache=TRUE, cache.lazy=FALSE}
#We extracted all transposases.
carpetaGENBANK <- "Datos/genomas/GENBANK"
archivosGENBANK <- list.files(carpetaGENBANK, pattern = "\\.gbk$", full.names = TRUE)
archivosGENBANK <- archivosGENBANK[!str_extract(basename(archivosGENBANK), "^[^_]+") %in% muestras_excluidas]

transposasas_gbk <- lapply(archivosGENBANK, function(archivo) {
  
  lineas <- readLines(archivo)
  muestra <- basename(archivo)
  resultados <- list()
  contig_actual <- NA
  i <- 1
  
  while (i <= length(lineas)) {
    
    if (grepl("^LOCUS", lineas[i])) {
      contig_actual <- gsub("^LOCUS\\s+(\\S+).*", "\\1", lineas[i])
    }
    
    if (grepl("^     CDS ", lineas[i])) {
      
      coords <- gsub(".*CDS\\s+", "", lineas[i])
      strand <- ifelse(grepl("complement", coords), "-", "+")
      coords <- gsub("complement\\(|\\)|join\\(", "", coords)
      coords <- trimws(coords)
      start <- gsub("\\..*", "", coords)
      end   <- gsub(".*\\.\\.", "", coords)
      
      locus_tag <- NA
      product   <- NA
      j <- i + 1
      
      while (j <= length(lineas) && grepl("^\\s{20}", lineas[j])) {
        if (grepl("/locus_tag=", lineas[j]))
          locus_tag <- gsub('.*locus_tag="([^"]+)".*', "\\1", lineas[j])
        if (grepl("/product=", lineas[j]))
          product <- gsub('.*product="([^"]+)".*', "\\1", lineas[j])
        j <- j + 1
      }
      
      if (!is.na(product) && grepl("transposase", product, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        resultados[[length(resultados) + 1]] <- data.frame(
          Muestra = muestra, contig = contig_actual, locus_tag = locus_tag,
          product = product, start = start, end = end, strand = strand
        )
      }
      i <- j
    } else {
      i <- i + 1
    }
  }
  
  if (length(resultados) > 0) bind_rows(resultados) else NULL
  
}) |> bind_rows()

cat("Total raw transposases:", nrow(transposasas_gbk), "\n")


#Add length
trans <- transposasas_gbk |>
  mutate(
    start    = as.integer(start),
    end      = as.integer(end),
    longitud = end - start + 1
  )

#FILTER: malformed product annotation (InsK)
mal_formateados <- trans |> filter(grepl('/product=|^\\s{20}', product))
cat("Malformed product annotation:", nrow(mal_formateados), "\n")

trans <- trans |>
  mutate(product = ifelse(
    grepl('^\\s*/product=', product),
    "Putative transposase InsK for insertion sequence",
    product
  ))

cat("Malformed after cleaning:", sum(grepl('^\\s*/product=', trans$product)), "\n")

#Family column
trans <- trans |>
  mutate(familia = case_when(
    grepl("family", product, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ gsub("^(\\S+)\\s+family.*", "\\1", product),
    TRUE ~ product
  ))
 
trans %>%
  dplyr::slice_sample(n = 5) %>%
  mutate(
    Muestra = str_extract(Muestra, "^[^_]+"),
    product = str_trunc(product, 40),
    familia = str_trunc(familia, 30)
  ) %>%
  select(Muestra, contig, locus_tag, familia, product, start, end, strand, longitud) %>%
  knitr::kable(
  caption = "Example of identified transposases (random sample of 5)",
  col.names = c("Strain", "Contig", "Locus tag", "Family", "Product", "Start", "End", "Strand", "Length")
)
```

We processes all GenBank files to extract information from annotated CDSs, including their locus tag, product, genomic coordinates, contig, and strand. We extracted 135177 CDSs.

```{r Extraction of CDSs, cache=TRUE, cache.lazy=FALSE}
#Extraction of CDSs
todos_cds <- lapply(archivosGENBANK, function(archivo) {
  
  lineas <- readLines(archivo)
  muestra <- basename(archivo)
  resultados <- list()
  contig_actual <- NA
  i <- 1
  
  while (i <= length(lineas)) {
    
    if (grepl("^LOCUS", lineas[i])) {
      contig_actual <- gsub("^LOCUS\\s+(\\S+).*", "\\1", lineas[i])
    }
    
    if (grepl("^     CDS ", lineas[i])) {
      
      coords <- gsub(".*CDS\\s+", "", lineas[i])
      strand <- ifelse(grepl("complement", coords), "-", "+")
      coords <- gsub("complement\\(|\\)|join\\(", "", coords)
      coords <- trimws(coords)
      start <- gsub("\\..*", "", coords)
      end   <- gsub(".*\\.\\.", "", coords)
      
      locus_tag <- NA
      product   <- NA
      j <- i + 1
      
      while (j <= length(lineas) && grepl("^\\s{20}", lineas[j])) {
        if (grepl("/locus_tag=", lineas[j]))
          locus_tag <- gsub('.*locus_tag="([^"]+)".*', "\\1", lineas[j])
        if (grepl("/product=", lineas[j]))
          product <- gsub('.*product="([^"]+)".*', "\\1", lineas[j])
        j <- j + 1
      }
      
      if (!is.na(locus_tag)) {
        resultados[[length(resultados) + 1]] <- data.frame(
          Muestra   = muestra,
          contig    = contig_actual,
          locus_tag = locus_tag,
          product   = product,
          start     = as.integer(start),
          end       = as.integer(end),
          strand    = strand
        )
      }
      i <- j
    } else {
      i <- i + 1
    }
  }
  
  if (length(resultados) > 0) bind_rows(resultados) else NULL
  
}) |> bind_rows()

cat("Total CDSs extracted:", nrow(todos_cds), "\n")
```

 
```{r}
# DETECTING TRANSPOSASES SPLIT BY A TRANSLATIONAL FRAMESHIFT

# Some IS families (IS3, IS1) express their active transposase from two overlapping reading frames (orfA/orfB), fused by a translational frameshift: the ribosome skips one nucleotide and continues in the other frame. Prokka/Prodigal do not model this skip, causing two problems seen in our data:

# CASE A - Transposase counted twice: both halves are named as a transposase and both end up in the table, so one real insertion is counted as two elements, each with half the true length.

# CASE B - Phantom neighbour: only one half is named as a transposase; the other, matching no known domain, is left as "hypothetical protein". It isn't counted as a transposase, but it is still a row in `todos_cds`, so the nearest-neighbour search picks it up as a real neighbour when it's actually the rest of the same protein.


# Families in which this mechanism is documented
familias_riesgo <- c("IS3", "IS1")

# Helper table: family of each locus_tag already classified as a transposase
familia_por_locus <- trans %>% select(locus_tag, familia)

# Detection: pairs of near-adjacent CDS (same contig/strain/strand, a gap of a few bp) where at least one of the two is already in trans

posibles_pares <- todos_cds %>%
  arrange(Muestra, contig, start) %>%
  group_by(Muestra, contig) %>%
  mutate(
    start_sig   = lead(start),
    end_sig     = lead(end),
    strand_sig  = lead(strand),
    locus_sig   = lead(locus_tag),
    product_sig = lead(product),
    gap         = start_sig - end
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(strand == strand_sig, gap >= -5, gap <= 5) %>%
  filter(locus_tag %in% trans$locus_tag | locus_sig %in% trans$locus_tag)

# Case A
duplicados_transposasa <- posibles_pares %>%
  filter(locus_tag %in% trans$locus_tag, locus_sig %in% trans$locus_tag) %>%
  inner_join(familia_por_locus, by = "locus_tag") %>%
  inner_join(familia_por_locus %>% rename(locus_sig = locus_tag, familia_sig = familia),
             by = "locus_sig") %>%
  filter(familia %in% familias_riesgo, familia_sig %in% familias_riesgo, familia == familia_sig)

# Case B
contaminacion_vecino <- posibles_pares %>%
  filter(xor(locus_tag %in% trans$locus_tag, locus_sig %in% trans$locus_tag)) %>%
  mutate(locus_transposasa = ifelse(locus_tag %in% trans$locus_tag, locus_tag, locus_sig)) %>%
  inner_join(familia_por_locus, by = c("locus_transposasa" = "locus_tag")) %>%
  filter(familia %in% familias_riesgo)

cat("Case A - duplicated transposases:", nrow(duplicados_transposasa), "\n")
dplyr::count(duplicados_transposasa, familia, sort = TRUE)

cat("\nCase B - phantom neighbours:", nrow(contaminacion_vecino), "\n")
dplyr::count(contaminacion_vecino, familia, sort = TRUE)

# Case A correction: merge each pair into a single row with the full coordinates, and remove the leftover half
fusiones <- duplicados_transposasa %>%
  transmute(
    Muestra, contig,
    locus_tag_fusion    = locus_tag,
    locus_tag_absorbido = locus_sig,
    start_nuevo = pmin(start, start_sig),
    end_nuevo   = pmax(end, end_sig)
  )

trans_original <- trans  

trans <- trans %>%
  filter(!locus_tag %in% fusiones$locus_tag_absorbido) %>%
  left_join(fusiones %>% select(locus_tag_fusion, start_nuevo, end_nuevo),
            by = c("locus_tag" = "locus_tag_fusion")) %>%
  mutate(
    start    = ifelse(!is.na(start_nuevo), start_nuevo, start),
    end      = ifelse(!is.na(end_nuevo), end_nuevo, end),
    longitud = end - start + 1
  ) %>%
  select(-start_nuevo, -end_nuevo)

cat("\nTransposases in trans - before:", nrow(trans_original), "after:", nrow(trans), "\n")

# Case B correction: remove the phantom fragment
locus_fantasma <- contaminacion_vecino %>%
  mutate(locus_fantasma = ifelse(locus_tag == locus_transposasa, locus_sig, locus_tag)) %>%
  dplyr::pull(locus_fantasma) %>%
  unique()

todos_cds_original <- todos_cds  

todos_cds <- todos_cds %>% filter(!locus_tag %in% locus_fantasma)

cat("CDSs in todos_cds - before:", nrow(todos_cds_original), "after:", nrow(todos_cds), "\n")


# Final check: abundance and median length of IS3/IS1 before and after the correction

bind_rows(
  trans_original %>% filter(familia %in% familias_riesgo) %>% mutate(estado = "antes"),
  trans          %>% filter(familia %in% familias_riesgo) %>% mutate(estado = "despues")
) %>%
  group_by(estado, familia) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mediana_bp = median(longitud), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(familia, estado)
```

For each of the 2342 identified transposases, the closest neighboring gene on each side (upstream and downstream) was identified within a maximum distance of 500 bp and on the same contig. Each transposase was also assigned the replicon type (chromosome or plasmid) of the contig in which it was located, based on the classification obtained with mlplasmids (Section 0).
 
 
```{r neighboring genes}
# Identify neighboring genes
distancia_max <- 500
vecinos <- lapply(1:nrow(trans), function(i) {
  
  tp <- trans[i, ]
  
# CDSs from the same contig and sample, excluding the transposase itself.

  cds_contig <- todos_cds |>
    filter(Muestra == tp$Muestra,
           contig  == tp$contig,
           locus_tag != tp$locus_tag)
  
# Upstream gene: the gene that ends closest before the start of the transposase.
  up <- cds_contig |>
    filter(end <= tp$start,
           (tp$start - end) <= distancia_max) |>
    arrange(desc(end)) |>
    slice(1)
  
# Downstream gene: the gene that starts closest after the end of the transposase.

  down <- cds_contig |>
    filter(start >= tp$end,
           (start - tp$end) <= distancia_max) |>
    arrange(start) |>
    slice(1)
  
  tp$upstream_product  <- if (nrow(up) > 0) up$product else NA
  tp$upstream_dist     <- if (nrow(up) > 0) tp$start - up$end else NA
  tp$upstream_locus_tag <- if (nrow(up) > 0) up$locus_tag else NA
  tp$downstream_product <- if (nrow(down) > 0) down$product else NA
  tp$downstream_locus_tag <- if (nrow(down) > 0) down$locus_tag else NA
  tp$downstream_dist    <- if (nrow(down) > 0) down$start - tp$end else NA
  
  tp
  
}) |> bind_rows()

cat("Transposases with upstream genes:", sum(!is.na(vecinos$upstream_product)), "\n")
cat("Transposases with downstream genes:", sum(!is.na(vecinos$downstream_product)), "\n")

# Correctly formatted products among upstream and downstream genes

vecinos <- vecinos |>
  mutate(
    upstream_product   = trimws(gsub('^\\s*/product="*', "", upstream_product)),
    downstream_product = trimws(gsub('^\\s*/product="*', "", downstream_product))
  )

cat("Malformed upstream products:", 
    sum(grepl('/product=', vecinos$upstream_product), na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Malformed downstream products:", 
    sum(grepl('/product=', vecinos$downstream_product), na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

# Chromosome/plasmid location added for each transposase

replicon_info <- mlplasmids_final |>
  select(contig_name, contig_length, prediction) |>
  rename(contig = contig_name,
         longitud_contig = contig_length,
         replicon = prediction)

vecinos <- vecinos |>
  left_join(replicon_info, by = "contig")

#Verify
cat("With assigned replicon:", sum(!is.na(vecinos$replicon)), "\n")
cat("Without an assigned replicon:", sum(is.na(vecinos$replicon)), "\n")

knitr::kable(
  vecinos |> dplyr::count(replicon, sort = TRUE),
  col.names = c("Replicon", "No. of transposases"),
  caption = "Number of transposases by replicon"
)

vecinos <- vecinos |>
  relocate(longitud_contig, replicon, .after = contig)

write_tsv(vecinos, "Resultados/vecinos_raw.tsv")

knitr::kable(
  vecinos %>% dplyr::slice_sample(n = 5),
  caption = "Random sample of 5 neighboring genes"
)
```

Starting from the `vecinos_raw.tsv` table (wide format, with upstream and downstream neighbors in separate columns for each transposase), a long-format version was generated, where each row represents a single transposase–neighbor relationship, indicating whether the neighbor is upstream or downstream. This resulted in 4,684 transposase–neighbor relationships from the 2,342 identified transposases. A filter was then applied to exclude mobile elements and mobility-associated proteins, as well as hypothetical proteins without functional annotation. After filtering, 1,244 functional neighbor relationships were retained for subsequent analyses.

```{r functional neighbors }
translong <- vecinos

# Keywords used to identify mobile elements and mobility-associated proteins (to be excluded)

keywords_moviles <- c(
  "transposase", "insertion sequence", "integrase",
  "resolvase", "transposon", "rep-associated")

es_movil <- function(x) {
  str_detect(str_to_lower(x), paste(keywords_moviles, collapse = "|"))
}

# Conversion from wide to long format — each row represents a transposase–neighbor–sample relationship

trans_long <- translong %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(upstream_product, downstream_product),
    names_to  = "posicion",
    values_to = "gen_vecino"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    posicion     = if_else(posicion == "upstream_product", "upstream", "downstream"),
    locus_vecino = if_else(posicion == "upstream", upstream_locus_tag, downstream_locus_tag),
    distancia    = if_else(posicion == "upstream", upstream_dist, downstream_dist)
  ) %>%
  select(Muestra, contig, replicon, familia, locus_tag, start,
         end, product, posicion, gen_vecino, locus_vecino, distancia)

# Save unfiltered long-format data

write_tsv(trans_long, "Resultados/vecinos_LONG_raw.tsv")

# Filter: remove mobile elements, mobility-associated proteins and hypothetical proteins

transfun_long <- trans_long %>%
  filter(!es_movil(gen_vecino),
         str_to_lower(gen_vecino) != "hypothetical protein")

cat("Total transposase–neighbor relationships (long format):", nrow(trans_long), "\n")
cat("Total functional neighbor relationships after filtering:", nrow(transfun_long), "\n")

# Data are in long format, with up to two rows per transposase (upstream/downstream). Save filtered long-format data

write_tsv(transfun_long, "Resultados/vecinosfun_long.tsv")

transfun_long %>%
  dplyr::slice_sample(n = 5) %>%
  mutate(
    Muestra    = str_extract(Muestra, "^[^_]+"),
    familia    = str_trunc(familia, 20),
    product    = str_trunc(product, 25),
    gen_vecino = str_trunc(gen_vecino, 25)
  ) %>%
 knitr::kable(
  caption = "Example of transposase–functional neighbor relationships (random sample of 5)",
  col.names = c("Strain", "Contig", "Replicon", "Family", "Locus tag", "Start", "End",
                "Product", "Position", "Neighboring gene", "Neighbor locus tag", "Distance")
)
```
 
## 2. Genomic composition of the strains
The 28 *E. coli* strains analyzed show variable total genome sizes, with substantial differences in the number and size of plasmids. The top panel shows the total genome size for each strain (chromosome + plasmids), ordered from largest to smallest. The bottom panel zooms in on the plasmids to facilitate comparison of their sizes. Labels indicate the number of plasmid-derived contigs per strain (p).

```{r genomic composition, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
contigs <- mlplasmids_final %>%
  transmute(
    Prediction    = prediction,
    Contig_name   = contig_name,
    Contig_length = contig_length,
    cepa          = muestra
  )

contigs_clean <- contigs %>% filter(!is.na(Contig_length), Contig_length > 0)

n_plasmidos <- contigs_clean %>%
  filter(Prediction == "Plasmid") %>%
  group_by(cepa) %>%
  summarise(n_plasmidos = n_distinct(Contig_name), .groups = "drop")

orden_cepas <- contigs_clean %>%
  group_by(cepa) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(Contig_length), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total)) %>%
  dplyr::pull(cepa)

total_por_cepa <- contigs_clean %>%
  group_by(cepa) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(Contig_length), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(n_plasmidos, by = "cepa") %>%
  mutate(n_plas = replace_na(n_plasmidos, 0),
         cepa = factor(cepa, levels = orden_cepas))

contigs_indiv <- contigs_clean %>%
  mutate(cepa = factor(cepa, levels = orden_cepas)) %>%
  arrange(cepa, Prediction, desc(Contig_length)) %>%
  group_by(cepa) %>%
  mutate(plasmid_rank = ifelse(Prediction == "Plasmid",
                               cumsum(Prediction == "Plasmid"), NA_integer_)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(segmento = case_when(
    Prediction == "Chromosome" ~ "Chromosome contig",
    TRUE ~ paste0("Plasmid contig ", plasmid_rank)
  )) %>%
  mutate(segmento = factor(segmento,
                           levels = c("Chromosome contig", paste0("Plasmid contig ", 1:max(plasmid_rank, na.rm = TRUE)))))

colores_plas <- c(
  "Chromosome contig" = "#2E86AB",
  "Plasmid contig 1"  = "#E84855",
  "Plasmid contig 2"  = "#F4A261",
  "Plasmid contig 3"  = "#2A9D8F",
  "Plasmid contig 4"  = "#8338EC",
  "Plasmid contig 5"  = "#FB5607",
  "Plasmid contig 6"  = "#FFBE0B",
  "Plasmid contig 7"  = "#3A86FF"
)

ymax <- max(total_por_cepa$total) / 1e6

# Top panel: complete genome
p_top <- ggplot(contigs_indiv, aes(x = cepa, y = Contig_length / 1e6, fill = segmento)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(data = total_por_cepa,
            aes(x = cepa, y = total / 1e6 + 0.05,
                label = ifelse(n_plas > 0, paste0(n_plas, "p"), "")),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.5, angle = 90, hjust = 0, color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colores_plas) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, ceiling(ymax) + 0.5, by = 0.5),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12)),
                     limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Genome size (Mb)", fill = "Replicon") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

# Bottom panel: plasmid zoom
p_bot <- ggplot(contigs_indiv %>% filter(Prediction == "Plasmid"),
                aes(x = cepa, y = Contig_length / 1e6, fill = segmento)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colores_plas) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 0.5, by = 0.1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
                     limits = c(0, 0.65)) +
  labs(x = "Strain", y = "Plasmid size (Mb)", fill = "Replicon") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"))

# Combine with patchwork
p_top / p_bot +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Genome size by strain",
    subtitle = "Top: complete genome | Bottom: plasmid zoom",
    caption  = "Numbering reflects rank by size and does not indicate homology or correspondence between plasmid contigs.",
    theme    = theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  )
```

## 3. General characterization of transposases
We identified 23 transposase families across the 28 strains. The most abundant families in terms of element count are IS3 (710 elements), IS1 (439 elements), IS66 (178 elements), ISNCY (146 elements), and IS21 (136 elements). On the other hand, the families with the widest strain distribution are IS200/IS605, IS3, ISKra4, and ISNCY, which show up in all 28 strains. IS1 is found in 26 out of the 28 strains, while IS66 and IS21 appear in 25. Some families, like IS1380 and IS1595, are only present in a single strain, which suggests they might have been acquired recently or are specific to a particular lineage.

For this characterization, we used the unfiltered version of the transposase-neighbor dataset (vecinos_LONG_raw.tsv), not the filtered one. That's because the functional neighbor filter is applied to the neighboring gene, not to the transposase itself, if we used the filtered version, we'd risk losing transposases whose both upstream and downstream neighbors got filtered out because they're either mobile elements or hypothetical proteins. That would end up underestimating the actual number of families and elements we identified.

```{r caracterizacion-transposasas}
df <- read_tsv("Resultados/vecinos_LONG_raw.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# One row per transposase: the long format repeats each element once per neighbour
is_unicas <- df |>
  distinct(Muestra, locus_tag, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(cepa = str_extract(Muestra, "^[^_]+"))

# Shorter labels for the two annotations not resolved to a formal family
abbreviate_labels <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_replace("Putative transposase InsK for insertion sequence", "InsK (putative)") |>
    str_replace("REP-associated tyrosine transposase", "REP-tyrosine")
}

cat("Transposases:", nrow(is_unicas), "\n")
cat("Family groups:", n_distinct(is_unicas$familia), "\n\n")

# Per strain: element count, repertoire richness and density 
por_cepa <- is_unicas |>
  group_by(cepa) |>
  summarise(n_transposasas = n(),
            n_familias     = n_distinct(familia), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(qc_final_28 |> select(cepa = muestra, total_length_quast), by = "cepa") |>
  mutate(densidad_mb = n_transposasas / (total_length_quast / 1e6))

cat("Transposases per strain:\n")
print(summary(por_cepa$n_transposasas))

cat("\nFamily groups per strain:\n")
print(summary(por_cepa$n_familias))

cat("\nSpearman correlation, transposase count vs genome size:",
    round(cor(por_cepa$n_transposasas, por_cepa$total_length_quast,
              method = "spearman"), 3), "\n\n")


por_cepa |> arrange(n_transposasas) |> slice(1, n()) |> print()

# Per family: abundance and prevalence 
por_familia <- is_unicas |>
  group_by(familia) |>
  summarise(n_elementos = n(), n_muestras = n_distinct(Muestra), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(n_elementos))

cat("\nThe five most abundant groups account for",
    round(100 * sum(head(por_familia$n_elementos, 5)) / nrow(is_unicas), 1), "% of all elements\n")

knitr::kable(por_familia |> mutate(familia = abbreviate_labels(familia)),
             caption = "Abundance and prevalence of each transposase family",
             col.names = c("Family", "Elements", "Strains (n = 28)"))

# IS5 concentrated in two strains
is_unicas |>
  dplyr::filter(familia == "IS5") |>
  dplyr::count(cepa, sort = TRUE) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "IS5 elements per strain",
               col.names = c("Strain", "Elements"))

```

```{r heatmap-recuentos, fig.height=7, fig.width=9}
mat_n <- conteos |>
```

## 4. Transposase distribution by replicon
Each transposase inherits the replicon of the contig it lies in, as assigned by mlplasmids. Absolute counts are not informative on their own, since the chromosome is much larger and is therefore expected to accumulate more elements. The analysis is based instead on density — transposases per megabase of replicon — computed as one value per strain and replicon, which is also the unit required by the pseudoreplication control described in the Methods.

Because both measurements come from the same strain, the comparison is paired: a Wilcoxon signed-rank test with the matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation as effect size.

Finally, the analysis asks whether replicon preference depends on the family. For each family with at least 20 elements, the proportion of its copies located on plasmids is compared with the overall proportion in the dataset, shown as a reference line.
 
Note that mlplasmids classifies individual contigs, so "plasmid" here refers to plasmid-predicted contigs rather than to complete plasmids.

```{r reparto-replicon}
# mlplasmids classifies contigs, not complete replicons: "Plasmid" here means plasmid-predicted contigs.
total_replicon <- is_unicas |>
  dplyr::mutate(tipo = ifelse(stringr::str_detect(replicon,
                              stringr::regex("plasmid", ignore_case = TRUE)),
                              "Plasmid", "Chromosome")) |>
  dplyr::count(tipo, name = "n") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))

knitr::kable(total_replicon,
             caption = "Transposases by contig replicon type",
             col.names = c("Replicon type", "Transposases", "%"))
```

```{r densidad-replicon}
# Total length of chromosomal and plasmid-predicted contigs in each strain
longitudes <- mlplasmids_final |>
  dplyr::mutate(tipo = ifelse(stringr::str_detect(prediction,
                              stringr::regex("plasmid", ignore_case = TRUE)),
                              "Plasmid", "Chromosome")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(muestra, tipo) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mb = sum(contig_length) / 1e6, .groups = "drop")

# Transposases per strain and replicon type
conteo_rep <- is_unicas |>
  dplyr::mutate(tipo = ifelse(stringr::str_detect(replicon,
                              stringr::regex("plasmid", ignore_case = TRUE)),
                              "Plasmid", "Chromosome")) |>
  dplyr::count(cepa, tipo, name = "n")

# Density: one value per strain and replicon type
densidad <- longitudes |>
  dplyr::rename(cepa = muestra) |>
  dplyr::left_join(conteo_rep, by = c("cepa", "tipo")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(n = tidyr::replace_na(n, 0),
                densidad = n / mb)

densidad |>
  dplyr::group_by(tipo) |>
  dplyr::summarise(strains = dplyr::n(),
                   median  = round(median(densidad), 1),
                   min     = round(min(densidad), 1),
                   max     = round(max(densidad), 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Transposase density per replicon type (elements per Mb of chromosomal or plasmid-predicted contigs)",
               col.names = c("Replicon type", "Strains", "Median", "Min", "Max"))
```

```{r test-densidad-replicon}
comp <- densidad |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = cepa, names_from = tipo, values_from = densidad) |>
  tidyr::drop_na()

cat("Strains with contigs of both replicon types:", nrow(comp), "\n")
cat("Strains where plasmid-contig density exceeds chromosomal density:",
    sum(comp$Plasmid > comp$Chromosome), "\n\n")

w <- wilcox.test(comp$Plasmid, comp$Chromosome, paired = TRUE)
print(w)

# Matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation as effect size
d <- comp$Plasmid - comp$Chromosome
r_rb_rep <- sum(sign(d) * rank(abs(d))) / sum(rank(abs(d)))
cat("\nMatched-pairs rank-biserial correlation:", round(r_rb_rep, 3), "\n")
```

```{r figura densidad replicon, fig.height=5, fig.width=4}
densidad |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tipo, y = densidad)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = cepa), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = tipo), size = 2.2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(begin = 0.2, end = 0.75, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Transposases per Mb of contig")
```

```{r enriquecimiento familia replicon, fig.height=5, fig.width=6}
# Overall proportion of elements on plasmid-predicted contigs, used as reference
prop_global <- mean(stringr::str_detect(is_unicas$replicon,
                    stringr::regex("plasmid", ignore_case = TRUE)))

enriquecimiento <- is_unicas |>
  dplyr::mutate(tipo = ifelse(stringr::str_detect(replicon,
                              stringr::regex("plasmid", ignore_case = TRUE)),
                              "Plasmid", "Chromosome")) |>
  dplyr::count(familia, tipo) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tipo, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(total = Chromosome + Plasmid,
                prop_plasmid = Plasmid / total) |>
  dplyr::filter(total >= 20) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(prop_plasmid))

knitr::kable(enriquecimiento |>
               dplyr::mutate(familia = abbreviate_labels(familia),
                             prop_plasmid = round(100 * prop_plasmid, 1)),
             caption = "Proportion of elements located on plasmid-predicted contigs, by family (families with at least 20 elements)",
             col.names = c("Family", "Chromosome", "Plasmid", "Total", "% on plasmid contigs"))

ggplot(enriquecimiento, aes(x = reorder(familia, prop_plasmid), y = prop_plasmid)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#21908C") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = prop_global, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = abbreviate_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "IS family", y = "Proportion of elements on plasmid-predicted contigs")
```

## 5. Transposase element length
Element length is taken as the length of the coding sequence annotated as a transposase, computed as end − start + 1. It therefore reflects the annotated gene rather than the complete insertion sequence, an important distinction for families whose elements encode more than one open reading frame.

Lengths are first compared between families, and then between replicon types. As in the previous section, the replicon comparison is aggregated to one median value per strain and replicon before testing, and the test is paired because both values come from the same strain.

Because plasmids and chromosomes differ in family composition, any overall length difference between replicon types could be a compositional artefact. Length is therefore also examined within each of the most abundant families separately, to distinguish a genuine replicon effect from a difference in which families are present.

```{r tam replicon}
size_IS <- df |>
  dplyr::mutate(cepa = stringr::str_extract(Muestra, "^[^_]+"),
                type = ifelse(stringr::str_detect(replicon,
                              stringr::regex("plasmid", ignore_case = TRUE)),
                              "Plasmid", "Chromosome"),
                size_pb = end - start + 1) |>
  dplyr::distinct(cepa, locus_tag, type, size_pb)

size_IS |>
  dplyr::group_by(type) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
                   mean   = round(mean(size_pb), 1),
                   median = round(median(size_pb), 1),
                   sd     = round(sd(size_pb), 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Transposase size (bp) by replicon type — element level",
               col.names = c("Replicon type", "Elements", "Mean", "Median", "SD"))

# Aggregation per strain to avoid pseudoreplication 
size_by_strain <- size_IS |>
  dplyr::group_by(cepa, type) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_size = median(size_pb), n_IS = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

size_by_strain |>
  dplyr::group_by(type) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_strains = dplyr::n(),
                   mean   = round(mean(median_size), 1),
                   median = round(median(median_size), 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Per-strain median transposase size (bp) by replicon type",
               col.names = c("Replicon type", "Strains", "Mean", "Median"))

# Normality of the aggregated values
shapiro_size <- size_by_strain |>
  dplyr::group_by(type) |>
  dplyr::summarise(W       = shapiro.test(median_size)$statistic,
                   p_value = shapiro.test(median_size)$p.value,
                   normal  = ifelse(shapiro.test(median_size)$p.value >= 0.05, "Yes", "No"),
                   .groups = "drop")

shapiro_size |>
  dplyr::mutate(p_value = format(p_value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Shapiro-Wilk test: normality of per-strain median size by replicon type")

# Paired comparison: both values come from the same strain 
comp_size <- size_by_strain |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = cepa, names_from = type, values_from = median_size) |>
  tidyr::drop_na()

wsize <- wilcox.test(comp_size$Plasmid, comp_size$Chromosome, paired = TRUE)
print(wsize)

d_size <- comp_size$Plasmid - comp_size$Chromosome
r_rb_size <- sum(sign(d_size) * rank(abs(d_size))) / sum(rank(abs(d_size)))

cat("\nStrains compared:", nrow(comp_size), "\n")
cat("Strains where plasmid elements are larger:", sum(d_size > 0), "\n")
cat("Matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation:", round(r_rb_size, 3), "\n")
```

## 6. Neighboring genes of transposases
To characterize the genomic context of transposases beyond family and replicon, we classified their immediate upstream and downstream neighbors — within 500 bp — into four categories: another transposase, a hypothetical protein, a characterized protein, or no neighbor when no gene was found within that distance, for example at a contig edge or across a large intergenic region. Because neighbor category and replicon type are both categorical variables, we assessed their association using a chi-squared test of independence on the resulting contingency table. We compared this classification between chromosomal and plasmid-predicted contigs, and identified which specific genes recur most frequently as neighbors in each replicon.

```{r resumen vecinos replicon}
# Classify each neighboring gene into 4 categories and split by replicon
resumen_vecinos <- df %>%
  mutate(
    # Chromosome vs Plasmid
    type = ifelse(str_detect(replicon, regex("plasmid", ignore_case = TRUE)),
                  "Plasmid", "Chromosome"),
    # Category of the neighboring gene
    neighbor_category = case_when(
      is.na(gen_vecino)                                                        ~ "No neighbor",
      str_detect(gen_vecino, regex("transpos|insertion|IS\\d|integrase",
                                   ignore_case = TRUE))                        ~ "Transposase",
      str_detect(gen_vecino, regex("hypothetical protein",
                                   ignore_case = TRUE))                        ~ "Hypothetical protein",
      TRUE                                                                     ~ "Characterized protein"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Count by replicon and category (each transposase contributes 2 positions: upstream and downstream)
  group_by(type, neighbor_category) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Calculate percentage within each replicon
  group_by(type) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
knitr::kable(resumen_vecinos, caption = "Neighboring positions by type, per replicon")
```

```{r test vecinos replicon}
  tibble::column_to_rownames("type") %>%
  as.matrix()

chisq.test(cont_table_1)
```

## 7. Functional classification of the transposase neighborhood
To characterize the type of genes flanking transposases, all functional neighboring genes (hypothetical proteins excluded) were classified into seven categories according to function. The antibiotic resistance category was identified using the Resistance Gene Identifier (RGI), the official tool of the CARD database. The protein sequences of the 2340 non-hypothetical neighboring genes were extracted from the 28 GenBank files and analyzed with RGI 6.0.5 (CARD 4.0.1) in protein mode, using DIAMOND-based homology detection and CARD's curated bitscore cutoffs (Perfect + Strict criterion).

Sequence-homology-based identification was chosen over gene-name matching to avoid the mismatch between Prokka's descriptive nomenclature and CARD's technical identifiers; RGI compares protein sequences directly against CARD models, so the original annotation does not bias the result. Hits were then cross-referenced with each locus's Prokka product name to integrate them into the rest of the analysis.

Antibiotic resistance was the only category validated against a curated database, since it bears directly on this thesis's central question and CARD is the field-standard resource for that purpose. The remaining six categories describe the broader functional landscape rather than testing a specific hypothesis, and were assigned from curated keyword sets applied to each gene's Prokka annotation and best read as a descriptive summary rather than a validated classification. Because functional category and replicon type are both categorical variables, we assessed their association using a chi-squared test of independence, applying Fisher's exact test with Monte Carlo simulation instead when expected cell counts were low."

```{r vecinos candidatos}
# Candidate neighbors (no hypothetical, no duplicates per strain)
vec_raw <- trans_long %>%
  filter(!is.na(locus_vecino), !is.na(gen_vecino),
         !grepl("hypothetical protein", gen_vecino, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(cepa = str_extract(Muestra, "^[^_]+")) %>%
  distinct(cepa, locus_vecino, gen_vecino, replicon)
```

```{r extraer prot vecinas, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Extract protein sequences from the .gbk files
extraer_proteinas <- function(gbk_path) {
  cepa <- str_extract(basename(gbk_path), "^[^_]+")
  loci <- vec_raw %>% filter(cepa == !!cepa) %>% dplyr::pull(locus_vecino) %>% unique()
  if (length(loci) == 0) return(tibble())
  contenido <- paste(readLines(gbk_path, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
  bloques   <- str_split(contenido, "\n     CDS ")[[1]][-1]
  map_dfr(bloques, function(b) {
    locus_m <- str_match(b, '/locus_tag="([^"]+)"')[,2]
    if (is.na(locus_m) || !(locus_m %in% loci)) return(NULL)
    trans_m <- str_match(b, '/translation="([^"]+)"')[,2]
    if (is.na(trans_m)) return(NULL)
    tibble(cepa, locus_tag = locus_m, seq = str_remove_all(trans_m, "\\s+"))
  })
}
proteinas <- map_dfr(archivosGENBANK, extraer_proteinas)
cat("Extracted proteins:", nrow(proteinas), "\n")

# Export to FASTA (RGI input)
aa <- AAStringSet(proteinas$seq)
names(aa) <- paste(proteinas$cepa, proteinas$locus_tag, sep = "|")
writeXStringSet(aa, "Resultados/proteinas_vecinas_CARD.fasta")
```

```{r cargar rgi}
# Load RGI results (CARD 4.0.1, Perfect+Strict criterion)
# RGI names its output after the run date; read the single .txt file in the folder
archivo_rgi <- list.files("Resultados/Resultado_RGI", pattern = "\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(archivo_rgi) == 1)
rgi <- read_tsv(archivo_rgi, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Build hits_card from RGI
hits_card <- rgi %>%
  transmute(cepa       = str_extract(ORF_ID, "^[^|]+"),
            locus_tag  = str_trim(str_extract(ORF_ID, "(?<=\\|)\\S+")),
            card_name  = Best_Hit_ARO,
            cutoff     = Cut_Off,
            drug_class = `Drug Class`,
            mechanism  = `Resistance Mechanism`) %>%
  distinct()

cat("CARD hits (RGI):", nrow(hits_card), "\n")
cat("Unique genes:", n_distinct(hits_card$card_name), "\n")
cat("Strains with a hit:", n_distinct(hits_card$cepa), "/28\n")

# Cross-reference hits with the neighboring gene name
gen_vecino_card <- hits_card %>%
  left_join(vec_raw, by = c("cepa", "locus_tag" = "locus_vecino")) %>%
  distinct(gen_vecino) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gen_vecino)) %>%
  dplyr::pull(gen_vecino)
cat("Neighboring genes validated by CARD:", length(gen_vecino_card), "\n")
```
```{r tabla resistencia card}
tabla_resistencia_card <- hits_card %>%
  left_join(vec_raw, by = c("cepa", "locus_tag" = "locus_vecino")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gen_vecino)) %>%
  mutate(tipo = ifelse(str_detect(replicon, regex("plasmid", ignore_case = TRUE)),
                        "Plasmid", "Chromosome")) %>%
  group_by(card_name, drug_class, mechanism) %>%
  summarise(
    n_strains = n_distinct(cepa),
    replicons = paste(sort(unique(tipo)), collapse = " & "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_strains)) %>%
  mutate(drug_class = ifelse(str_count(drug_class, ";") + 1 > 3,
                              "Multidrug efflux",
                              drug_class))

write.csv2(tabla_resistencia_card, "Resultados/Table_1.csv", row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(tabla_resistencia_card,
             caption = "Antibiotic resistance genes identified among transposase neighbors (CARD/RGI, Perfect+Strict)",
             col.names = c("Gene", "Drug class", "Resistance mechanism", "N strains", "Replicon(s)"))
```

```{r vecindario funcional}
vecindario <- bind_rows(
  tabla_chr_filtrada %>% mutate(tipo = "Chromosome"),
  tabla_plas_filtrada %>% mutate(tipo = "Plasmid")
) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gen_vecino),
         !grepl("hypothetical protein", gen_vecino, ignore.case = TRUE),
         !grepl("insertion sequence|integrase|rep-associated", gen_vecino, ignore.case = TRUE))

clasificar_funcion <- function(gen) {
  case_when(
    # 1. Resistance — validated by homology against CARD v4.0.1
    gen %in% gen_vecino_card ~ "Resistance",
    # 2. Virulence and adherence
    grepl("fimbri|pilin|pilus|pili|adhesin|antigen 43|hemolysin|leukotoxin|serine protease Esp|serine protease sat|autotransporter|IcsA|surface presentation|Spa[OS]|colicin|virulence|VirB|VirF|HilA|invasion|pathogen|toxin secretion|type III|type IV secretion|PapC|PapE|PapG|FimD|FimF|FimG|fimbrial|S-fimbrial|PAP fimbrial|fimbrial adhesin",
          gen, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Virulence/Adherence",
    # 3. Toxin-antitoxin and SOS response
    grepl("toxic protein|antitoxin|endoribonuclease Pem|MqsA|CbeA|GhoS|orphan toxin|small toxic|UmuC|SOS response|DNA damage-inducible|ldr[A-Z]|Hok[A-Z]|PemK",
          gen, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Toxin-Antitoxin/SOS",
    # 4. Plasmid maintenance and mobility
    grepl("RepA|plasmid segregation|FlmC|fertility inhibition|TraD|TraI|TraY|TraC|TraQ|relaxosome|origin-binding|replicative DNA helicase|tyrosine recombinase|serine recombinase|prophage integrase|antirestriction|conjugation|mobilization|ParM|plasmid partition|StbB|conjugal transfer",
          gen, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Plasmid maintenance",
    # 5. Transcriptional regulation
    grepl("HTH-type|transcriptional regulator|transcriptional activator|transcriptional repressor|repressor|RNA polymerase sigma|H-NS|sensor protein|ArcA|two-component|regulatory protein|operon.*regul|regul.*operon",
          gen, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Regulation",
    # 6. Metabolism
    grepl("dehydrogenase|synthase|reductase|hydratase|transferase|aldolase|kinase|ligase|hydrolase|lyase|epimerase|phosphatase|oxidoreductase|enolase|permease|transporter|symporter|antiporter|decarboxylase|isomerase|mutase|carboxylase|synthetase|deaminase|hydroxylase|lactonase|racemase|dehydratase|methyltransferase|glucosyltransferase|glycosyltransferase|acetyltransferase|acyltransferase|aminotransferase|phosphorylase|esterase|peptidase|protease|nucleosidase|nucleotidase|lipase|sulfatase|desaturase|oxidase",
          gen, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Metabolism",
    # 7. Other functional
    TRUE ~ "Other functional"
  )
}

vecindario_clasificado <- vecindario %>%
  mutate(categoria = clasificar_funcion(gen_vecino),
         categoria = factor(categoria, levels = c(
           "Resistance", "Metabolism", "Regulation", "Other functional",
           "Toxin-Antitoxin/SOS", "Virulence/Adherence", "Plasmid maintenance"
         )))

vecindario_pct <- vecindario_clasificado %>%
  group_by(tipo, categoria) %>%
  summarise(total_ocurrencias = sum(n_ocurrencias), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(tipo) %>%
  mutate(pct = total_ocurrencias / sum(total_ocurrencias))

ggplot(vecindario_pct, aes(x = tipo, y = pct, fill = categoria)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(pct >= 0.01, scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 0.1), "")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 3.2, color = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Functional category") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Proportion of occurrences (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        legend.key.size = unit(0.45, "cm"),
        legend.text     = element_text(size = 9))
```

## 8. Transposase-associated hypomethylation — Dam methylome
To characterize the relationship between Dam methylation and transposases, we assessed hypomethylation within a defined window around each element. Sites with a methylation score ≤ 0.5 were considered hypomethylated. For each transposase, a ±200 bp window around its coordinates was defined, and every hypomethylated site within that window was classified as upstream, downstream, or intra according to its position relative to the element. Because the windows of nearby transposases can overlap, a single hypomethylated site may be associated with more than one transposase; counts therefore reflect site-transposase relationships rather than unique physical sites in the genome. In two of the 28 strains (DA63796, DA63960), replicon-level analyses showed very little or no hypomethylation signal in some regions, possibly due to a technical limitation in methylome generation for these samples; both strains are therefore underrepresented in the results that follow.

```{r cargar datos dam}
tsv_raw <- read_tsv("Resultados/vecinos_LONG_raw.tsv",
                    show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(cepa = str_extract(Muestra, "^[^_]+"))

ventanasmeti <- tsv_raw %>%
  distinct(cepa, locus_tag, start, end, contig, replicon, familia) %>%
  mutate(start_ext200 = start - 200,
         end_ext200 = end + 200)

vecinos_meti <- tsv_raw %>%
  select(cepa, locus_tag, posicion, gen_vecino, locus_vecino, distancia)
```

```{r parsear wig dam}
carpeta_wig <- "Datos/metilomas"
archivos_dam <- list.files(carpeta_wig, pattern = "_dam\\.dampened.*\\.wig$", full.names = TRUE)

# Parser: captures the contig (chrom=) of each block, vectorized
wig_dam <- map_dfr(archivos_dam, function(f) {
  cepa  <- str_extract(basename(f), "^[^_]+")
  hebra <- ifelse(grepl("plus", f), "+", "-")
  lineas <- readLines(f)
  es_header <- grepl("^variableStep", lineas)
  idx_header <- cumsum(es_header)
  chrom_por_bloque <- str_match(lineas[es_header], "chrom=(\\S+)")[, 2]
  chrom_por_bloque <- str_extract(chrom_por_bloque, "\\d+")
  contig_vec <- ifelse(idx_header > 0, chrom_por_bloque[idx_header], NA_character_)
  es_dato <- !es_header & !grepl("^track", lineas) & lineas != ""
  df <- read.table(text = lineas[es_dato], col.names = c("pos", "score"))
  df$contig_num <- contig_vec[es_dato]
  df$cepa  <- cepa
  df$hebra <- hebra
  df
}) %>%
  filter(score <= 0.5)
```

```{r cruce dam ventanas}
# Join: by strain + contig number (the wig's "1" matches the gbk's "_1")
resultado_dam <- wig_dam %>%
  inner_join(
    ventanasmeti %>% mutate(contig_num = str_extract(contig, "[0-9]+$")),
    by = c("cepa", "contig_num"),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  filter(pos >= start_ext200, pos <= end_ext200) %>%
  mutate(zona = case_when(
    pos < start ~ "upstream",
    pos > end   ~ "downstream",
    TRUE        ~ "intra"
  ))
```

```{r tabla zona replicon dam}
resultado_dam %>%
  dplyr::count(zona, replicon) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Dam hypomethylation by zone and replicon",
               col.names = c("Zone", "Replicon", "N"))
```

```{r figura zona replicon dam}
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +

  labs(x = "Zone", y = "N hypomethylations")
```

```{r vecinos regulatorios dam}
cepas_por_gen <- resultado_con_vecinos %>%
  filter(!is.na(gen_vecino),
         !grepl("transposase|transposon|invertase|hypothetical", gen_vecino, ignore.case = TRUE),
         zona != "intra") %>%
  group_by(gen_vecino, replicon) %>%
  summarise(n_cepas_total = n_distinct(cepa), .groups = "drop")

resultado_con_vecinos %>%
  filter(!is.na(gen_vecino),
         !grepl("transposase|transposon|invertase|hypothetical", gen_vecino, ignore.case = TRUE),
         zona != "intra") %>%
  group_by(gen_vecino, replicon, zona) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = zona, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  left_join(cepas_por_gen, by = c("gen_vecino", "replicon")) %>%
  mutate(total = upstream + downstream) %>%
  filter(n_cepas_total >= 2) %>%
  arrange(replicon, desc(n_cepas_total)) %>%
  select(gen_vecino, replicon, downstream, upstream, n_cepas_total, total) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Neighbor genes with regulatory hypomethylation (up/down) in at least 2 strains (dam)",
               col.names = c("Neighbor gene", "Replicon", "Downstream", "Upstream", "N strains", "Total"))
```

## 9. Transposase-associated hypomethylation — Dcm methylome
The same approach was applied to Dcm methylation, using the CCWGG motif and the same 0.5 score threshold and ±200 bp window definition described above. As with Dam, DA63796 and DA63960 remain underrepresented in the replicon-level analyses below. To compare the overall proportion of hypomethylation between chromosome and plasmid while controlling for pseudoreplication, data were first aggregated by strain, yielding one hypomethylation proportion per strain and replicon; because each strain contributes both a chromosome and a plasmid value, this comparison is inherently paired rather than between independent groups. A Shapiro-Wilk test showed that the hypomethylation proportion did not follow a normal distribution in either replicon (p<0.0001 for both), so a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used, together with the matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation as the effect size measure.

```{r parsear wig dcm}
archivos_dcm <- list.files(carpeta_wig, pattern = "_dcm\\.dampened.*\\.wig$", full.names = TRUE)

# Parser: captures the contig (chrom=) of each block
wig_dcm <- map_dfr(archivos_dcm, function(f) {
  cepa  <- str_extract(basename(f), "^[^_]+")
  hebra <- ifelse(grepl("plus", f), "+", "-")
  lineas <- readLines(f)
  es_header <- grepl("^variableStep", lineas)
  idx_header <- cumsum(es_header)
  chrom_por_bloque <- str_match(lineas[es_header], "chrom=(\\S+)")[, 2]
  chrom_por_bloque <- str_extract(chrom_por_bloque, "\\d+")
  contig_vec <- ifelse(idx_header > 0, chrom_por_bloque[idx_header], NA_character_)
  es_dato <- !es_header & !grepl("^track", lineas) & lineas != ""
  df <- read.table(text = lineas[es_dato], col.names = c("pos", "score"))
  df$contig_num <- contig_vec[es_dato]
  df$cepa  <- cepa
  df$hebra <- hebra
  df
}) %>%
  filter(score <= 0.5)
```

```{r cruce dcm ventanas}
# Join: by strain + contig number 
resultado_dcm <- wig_dcm %>%
  inner_join(
    ventanasmeti %>% mutate(contig_num = str_extract(contig, "[0-9]+$")),
    by = c("cepa", "contig_num"),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  filter(pos >= start_ext200, pos <= end_ext200) %>%
  mutate(zona = case_when(
    pos < start ~ "upstream",
    pos > end   ~ "downstream",
    TRUE        ~ "intra"
  ))
```

```{r figura hipo hiper enzima, warning=FALSE}
# Parser (not filtered: want all motifs)
leer_wig_full <- function(f) {
  cepa  <- str_extract(basename(f), "^[^_]+")
  hebra <- ifelse(grepl("plus", f), "+", "-")
  lineas <- readLines(f)
  es_header <- grepl("^variableStep", lineas)
  idx_header <- cumsum(es_header)
  chrom_por_bloque <- str_match(lineas[es_header], "chrom=(\\S+)")[, 2]
  chrom_por_bloque <- str_extract(chrom_por_bloque, "\\d+")
  contig_vec <- ifelse(idx_header > 0, chrom_por_bloque[idx_header], NA_character_)
  es_dato <- !es_header & !grepl("^track", lineas) & lineas != ""
  df <- read.table(text = lineas[es_dato], col.names = c("pos", "score"))
  df$contig_num <- contig_vec[es_dato]
  df$cepa  <- cepa
  df$hebra <- hebra
  df
}
wig_dam_full <- map_dfr(archivos_dam, leer_wig_full)
wig_dcm_full <- map_dfr(archivos_dcm, leer_wig_full)
ventanas_cn <- ventanasmeti %>% mutate(contig_num = str_extract(contig, "[0-9]+$"))

buscar_motivos_ventana <- function(wig_full) {
  map_dfr(unique(ventanas_cn$cepa), function(cc) {
    wig_full %>%
      filter(cepa == cc) %>%
      inner_join(filter(ventanas_cn, cepa == cc),
                 by = c("cepa", "contig_num"),
                 relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
      filter(pos >= start_ext200, pos <= end_ext200) %>%
      distinct(cepa, contig_num, pos, score, hebra, replicon)
  })
}
resultado_dam_full <- buscar_motivos_ventana(wig_dam_full)
resultado_dcm_full <- buscar_motivos_ventana(wig_dcm_full)

datos_hipo_hiper <- bind_rows(
  resultado_dam_full %>% mutate(enzima = "Dam"),
  resultado_dcm_full %>% mutate(enzima = "Dcm")
) %>%
  mutate(metilacion = ifelse(score <= 0.5, "Hypomethylated", "Hypermethylated")) %>%
  group_by(enzima, replicon, metilacion) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(enzima, replicon) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n))

ggplot(datos_hipo_hiper, aes(x = enzima, y = pct, fill = metilacion)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 0.1)),
            position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 3.5, color = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  facet_wrap(~replicon) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "") +
  labs(x = "Enzyme", y = "Proportion")
```

```{r}
# Per-strain aggregation to avoid pseudoreplication (same as section 5)
datos_hipo_hiper_cepa <- bind_rows(
  resultado_dam_full %>% mutate(enzima = "Dam"),
  resultado_dcm_full %>% mutate(enzima = "Dcm")
) %>%
  mutate(metilacion = ifelse(score <= 0.5, "Hypomethylated", "Hypermethylated")) %>%
  distinct(cepa, contig_num, pos, enzima, replicon, metilacion)

prop_hipo_cepa <- datos_hipo_hiper_cepa %>%
  group_by(cepa, replicon) %>%
  summarise(n_total   = n(),
            n_hipo    = sum(metilacion == "Hypomethylated"),
            prop_hipo = n_hipo / n_total,
            .groups = "drop")

prop_hipo_cepa %>%
  group_by(replicon) %>%
  summarise(n_strains = n(),
            mean   = round(mean(prop_hipo), 3),
            median = round(median(prop_hipo), 3)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Per-strain proportion of hypomethylated motifs by replicon")

# which strains have plasmid data here, only strains with data in BOTH replicons can be paired
prop_hipo_cepa %>% filter(replicon == "Plasmid") %>% dplyr::pull(cepa)

shapiro_hipo <- prop_hipo_cepa %>%
  group_by(replicon) %>%
  summarise(
    W       = shapiro.test(prop_hipo)$statistic,
    p_value = shapiro.test(prop_hipo)$p.value,
    normal  = ifelse(shapiro.test(prop_hipo)$p.value >= 0.05, "Yes", "No"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

shapiro_hipo %>%
  mutate(p_value = format(p_value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Shapiro-Wilk test: normality of per-strain hypomethylation proportion by replicon")

prop_hipo_wide <- prop_hipo_cepa %>%
  select(cepa, replicon, prop_hipo) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = replicon, values_from = prop_hipo) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Chromosome), !is.na(Plasmid))

whipo <- wilcox.test(prop_hipo_wide$Chromosome, prop_hipo_wide$Plasmid, paired = TRUE)

n_pairs <- nrow(prop_hipo_wide)

# Matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation from the V statistic
r_rb_hipo <- (4 * whipo$statistic) / (n_pairs * (n_pairs + 1)) - 1

data.frame(
  Test          = "Wilcoxon signed-rank (paired)",
  n_pairs       = n_pairs,
  V             = whipo$statistic,
  p_value       = format(whipo$p.value, scientific = TRUE),
  effect_size_r = round(r_rb_hipo, 2)
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Wilcoxon signed-rank test: Chromosome vs Plasmid (per-strain hypomethylation proportion, paired by strain)")
```

```{r Tabla_2}
  write.csv2("Resultados/Table_2.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## 10. Position of hypomethylated motifs: CDS vs regulatory region by family
For the three transposase families with the highest number of elements across strains (selected by actual element abundance, not by number of hypomethylation events, to avoid preselecting families based on the very variable of interest), each hypomethylated motif (score ≤ 0.5, Dam+Dcm) was classified according to its position relative to the element: within the coding region (CDS) or within its flanking regulatory window (±200 bp, upstream/downstream). The analysis was performed separately for chromosome and plasmid. Because the regulatory window has a fixed size (400 bp total) while CDS length varies across families, a longer element will accumulate more internal motifs in absolute terms purely as a size effect, even in the absence of any biological pattern; to control for this, the observed CDS percentage for each family was compared against the percentage expected by chance from its median length, assuming a uniform density of motifs per bp.

``` {r figura cds reg familia raw}
familias_sel <- c("IS3", "IS1", "IS66")
dam_cds_reg <- resultado_dam %>% mutate(enzima = "Dam")
dcm_cds_reg <- resultado_dcm %>% mutate(enzima = "Dcm")

cds_reg_plot <- bind_rows(dam_cds_reg, dcm_cds_reg) %>%
  filter(familia %in% familias_sel) %>%
  mutate(
    categoria = ifelse(zona == "intra", "CDS", "Regulatory (±200 bp)"),
    familia   = factor(familia, levels = familias_sel)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(familia, enzima, replicon, categoria)

ggplot(cds_reg_plot, aes(x = familia, y = n, fill = categoria)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.65),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  facet_grid(replicon ~ enzima) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "") +
  labs(x = "Family", y = "N hypomethylated motifs")
```


```{r}
# length by family to compare
ventanasmeti %>% 
  filter(familia %in% c("IS3", "IS1", "IS66")) %>% 
  group_by(familia) %>% 
  summarise(mediana_pb = median(end - start + 1), n = dplyr::n()) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median element length by family",
               col.names = c("Family", "Median length (bp)", "N elements"))
```

To test whether each family's regulatory-region enrichment exceeds what its length alone predicts, we compared observed regulatory events against the chance proportion expected from median element length (assuming uniform per-bp motif density), using an exact binomial test: first pooling both replicons (family-wide median), then separately by replicon (using each replicon's own median length, since plasmid-borne and chromosomal copies of the same family can differ substantially in size).
```{r test familia}
# Expected regulatory proportion for each family (pooled, used for the combined test)
medianas <- ventanasmeti %>% 
  filter(familia %in% c("IS3", "IS1", "IS66")) %>% 
  group_by(familia) %>% 
  summarise(mediana_pb = median(end - start + 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(p_esperado_reg = 400 / (mediana_pb + 400))

medianas

# test (chromosome + plasmid) 
datos_combinado <- tabla_cds_reg_combinado %>%
  group_by(familia) %>%
  summarise(
    n_reg   = n[categoria == "Regulatory (±200 bp)"],
    n_total = sum(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(medianas, by = "familia")

test_combinado <- pmap_dfr(datos_combinado, function(familia, n_reg, n_total, mediana_pb, p_esperado_reg) {
  bt <- binom.test(n_reg, n_total, p = p_esperado_reg)
  tibble(
    familia, n_reg, n_total, mediana_pb, p_esperado_reg,
    pct_observado = n_reg / n_total,
    p_valor = bt$p.value,
    ic95_inf = bt$conf.int[1],
    ic95_sup = bt$conf.int[2]
  )
})

test_combinado

# Expected regulatory proportion for each family, BY REPLICON 
medianas_replicon <- ventanasmeti %>%
  filter(familia %in% c("IS3", "IS1", "IS66")) %>%
  group_by(familia, replicon) %>%
  summarise(mediana_pb = median(end - start + 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(p_esperado_reg = 400 / (mediana_pb + 400))

medianas_replicon

# Test by replicon 
datos_replicon <- tabla_cds_reg_replicon %>%
  group_by(familia, replicon) %>%
  summarise(
    n_reg   = n[categoria == "Regulatory (±200 bp)"],
    n_total = sum(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(medianas_replicon, by = c("familia", "replicon"))

test_replicon <- pmap_dfr(datos_replicon, function(familia, replicon, n_reg, n_total, mediana_pb, p_esperado_reg) {
  bt <- binom.test(n_reg, n_total, p = p_esperado_reg)
  tibble(
    familia, replicon, n_reg, n_total, mediana_pb, p_esperado_reg,
    pct_observado = n_reg / n_total,
    p_valor = bt$p.value,
    ic95_inf = bt$conf.int[1],
    ic95_sup = bt$conf.int[2]
  )
})

test_replicon
```

## 11. Epigenetic context of resistance genes associated with transposases
To evaluate whether the hypomethylation associated with resistance genes is located within the gene itself or within its neighboring transposase, two parallel analysis windows were compared: one centered on the genomic coordinates of the resistance gene (the genes validated by CARD, see Section 7) and another centered on the adjacent transposase, both spanning ±200 base pairs and using the same hypomethylation threshold (methylation score ≤ 0.5) and the same distinction between coding sequence and regulatory region used in the preceding sections. For each gene and strain in which the gene is present, hypomethylation was assessed independently for the gene itself and for its nearest neighboring transposase, classifying each as absent, present with no hypomethylation, present with hypomethylation in the regulatory region, or present with hypomethylation within the coding sequence. Comparing these two independent classifications makes it possible to determine directly whether the epigenetic mark falls on the adaptive gene or on the mobile element that accompanies it.

### 11.1 Window centered on the resistance gene
```{r heatmap resistencia gen}
# Coordinates + contig of resistance genes from todos_cds 
resist_coords <- hits_card %>%
  left_join(
    todos_cds %>%
      mutate(cepa = str_extract(Muestra, "^[^_]+")) %>%
      select(cepa, locus_tag, contig, start_gen = start, end_gen = end),
    by = c("cepa", "locus_tag")
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(start_gen)) %>%
  mutate(
    contig_num = str_extract(contig, "[0-9]+$"),
    start_ext  = start_gen - 200,
    end_ext    = end_gen   + 200
  )

# by strain + contig_num
buscar_hipo <- function(wig_full, enzima_nombre) {
  wig_full %>%
    filter(score <= 0.5) %>%
    inner_join(resist_coords, by = c("cepa", "contig_num"),
               relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    filter(pos >= start_ext, pos <= end_ext) %>%
    mutate(zona = case_when(
      pos < start_gen ~ "upstream",
      pos > end_gen   ~ "downstream",
      TRUE            ~ "intra"
    )) %>%
    distinct(cepa, locus_tag, card_name, zona) %>%
    mutate(enzima = enzima_nombre)
}

hipo_dam <- buscar_hipo(wig_dam_full, "Dam")
hipo_dcm <- buscar_hipo(wig_dcm_full, "Dcm")
hipo_all <- bind_rows(hipo_dam, hipo_dcm)

todas_cepas <- orden_cepas
todos_genes  <- sort(unique(resist_coords$card_name))

estado_resist <- expand.grid(cepa = todas_cepas, card_name = todos_genes,
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(
    resist_coords %>% distinct(cepa, card_name) %>% mutate(presente = TRUE),
    by = c("cepa", "card_name")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    hipo_all %>%
      group_by(cepa, card_name) %>%
      summarise(
        hipo_reg = any(zona %in% c("upstream", "downstream")),
        hipo_cds = any(zona == "intra"),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = c("cepa", "card_name")
  ) %>%
  mutate(estado = case_when(
    is.na(presente)   ~ "Absent",
    hipo_cds  == TRUE ~ "Present + CDS hypo",
    hipo_reg  == TRUE ~ "Present + regulatory hypo",
    TRUE              ~ "Present, no hypomethylation"
  ),
  estado = factor(estado, levels = c(
    "Absent",
    "Present, no hypomethylation",
    "Present + regulatory hypo",
    "Present + CDS hypo"
  )))

# Table 
estado_resist %>%
  dplyr::count(estado) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Resistance gene status counts (gene-centered window, all strain-gene pairs)")

mat_R <- estado_resist %>%
  mutate(val = ifelse(estado == "Absent", 0, 1)) %>%
  group_by(cepa, card_name) %>%
  summarise(val = max(val), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = card_name, values_from = val, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("cepa") %>%
  as.matrix()

orden_cepas_R <- rownames(mat_R)[hclust(dist(mat_R,    method = "binary"))$order]
orden_genes_R <- colnames(mat_R)[hclust(dist(t(mat_R), method = "binary"))$order]

estado_resist_ord <- estado_resist %>%
  group_by(cepa, card_name) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = estado, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(cepa      = factor(cepa,      levels = orden_cepas_R),
         card_name = factor(card_name, levels = orden_genes_R))

# Absent left white 
colores_matriz <- c(
  "Absent"                       = "white",
  setNames(viridisLite::viridis(3),
           c("Present, no hypomethylation", "Present + regulatory hypo", "Present + CDS hypo"))
)

ggplot(estado_resist_ord, aes(x = card_name, y = cepa, fill = estado)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colores_matriz, name = "") +
  labs(
    title    = "Resistance epigenetic matrix (CARD)",
    subtitle = "Dam/Dcm hypomethylation within \u00b1200 bp window of the resistance gene",
    x        = "Resistance gene (CARD)",
    y        = "Strain"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position  = "top",
    legend.key.size  = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid       = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40")
  )
```

### 11.2 Window centered on the neighboring transposase
```{r heatmap resistencia transposasa}
# rename locus_tag to locus_tag_transposa to avoid the ambiguity when column names matched.
puente <- tsv_raw %>%
  mutate(cepa = str_extract(Muestra, "^[^_]+")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(locus_vecino)) %>%
  distinct(cepa,
           locus_tag_transposa = locus_tag,
           locus_vecino)

resist_con_transposa <- hits_card %>%
  inner_join(puente, by = c("cepa", "locus_tag" = "locus_vecino"))

# The transposase column is now called locus_tag_transposa and the resistance gene column remains locus_tag.
hipo_transposa <- bind_rows(dam_cds_reg, dcm_cds_reg) %>%
  distinct(cepa, locus_tag, zona, enzima)

# join uses locus_tag_transposa not locus_tag.y
resist_hipo_A <- resist_con_transposa %>%
  left_join(hipo_transposa,
            by = c("cepa", "locus_tag_transposa" = "locus_tag"),
            relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  group_by(cepa, card_name) %>%
  summarise(
    hipo_reg = any(zona %in% c("upstream", "downstream"), na.rm = TRUE),
    hipo_cds = any(zona == "intra", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

estado_resist_A <- expand.grid(cepa = orden_cepas,
                                card_name = sort(unique(hits_card$card_name)),
                                stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(
    hits_card %>% distinct(cepa, card_name) %>% mutate(presente = TRUE),
    by = c("cepa", "card_name")
  ) %>%
  left_join(resist_hipo_A, by = c("cepa", "card_name")) %>%
  mutate(estado = case_when(
    is.na(presente)   ~ "Absent",
    hipo_cds == TRUE  ~ "Present + CDS hypo (transposase)",
    hipo_reg == TRUE  ~ "Present + regulatory hypo (transposase)",
    TRUE              ~ "Present, no hypomethylation"
  ),
  estado = factor(estado, levels = c(
    "Absent",
    "Present, no hypomethylation",
    "Present + regulatory hypo (transposase)",
    "Present + CDS hypo (transposase)"
  )))

# Table 
estado_resist_A %>%
  dplyr::count(estado) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Resistance gene status counts (neighboring-transposase window, all strain-gene pairs)")

mat_A <- estado_resist_A %>%
  mutate(val = ifelse(estado == "Absent", 0, 1)) %>%
  group_by(cepa, card_name) %>%
  summarise(val = max(val), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = card_name, values_from = val, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("cepa") %>%
  as.matrix()

orden_cepas_A <- rownames(mat_A)[hclust(dist(mat_A,    method = "binary"))$order]
orden_genes_A <- colnames(mat_A)[hclust(dist(t(mat_A), method = "binary"))$order]

estado_resist_A_ord <- estado_resist_A %>%
  group_by(cepa, card_name) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = estado, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(cepa      = factor(cepa,      levels = orden_cepas_A),
         card_name = factor(card_name, levels = orden_genes_A))

# Absent left white
colores_A <- c(
  "Absent"                                   = "white",
  setNames(viridisLite::viridis(3),
           c("Present, no hypomethylation",
             "Present + regulatory hypo (transposase)",
             "Present + CDS hypo (transposase)"))
)

ggplot(estado_resist_A_ord, aes(x = card_name, y = cepa, fill = estado)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colores_A, name = "") +
  labs(
    title    = "Resistance epigenetic matrix (CARD)",
    subtitle = "Dam/Dcm hypomethylation within \u00b1200 bp window of the neighboring transposase",
    x = "Resistance gene (CARD)", y = "Strain"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
```

```{r tabla comparacion resistencia}
comparacion_resist <- estado_resist_ord %>%
  select(cepa, card_name, estado_gen = estado) %>%
  inner_join(
    estado_resist_A_ord %>% select(cepa, card_name, estado_transposa = estado),

table(comparacion_resist$estado_gen, comparacion_resist$estado_transposa) %>%

# Cases where the gene IS hypomethylated but its neighboring transposase is NOT
comparacion_resist %>%
  filter(estado_gen == "Present + CDS hypo",
         estado_transposa == "Present, no hypomethylation") %>%
  select(cepa, card_name) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Genes with own hypomethylation but non-hypomethylated neighboring transposase")

# Cases where the neighboring transposase IS hypomethylated but the gene NOT
comparacion_resist %>%
  filter(estado_gen == "Present, no hypomethylation",
         estado_transposa %in% c("Present + CDS hypo (transposase)", "Present + regulatory hypo (transposase)")) %>%
  select(cepa, card_name, estado_transposa) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Genes with non-hypomethylated own gene but hypomethylated neighboring transposase")
```

## 12. Epigenetic context of the functional neighborhood of transposases
The two-window comparison of Section 11 was extended from CARD-validated resistance genes to all neighbouring genes in the four adaptive categories (Resistance, Virulence/Adherence, Toxin-Antitoxin/SOS and Plasmid maintenance). Only regulatory hypomethylation (upstream or downstream, excluding the coding sequence) was considered, and each case corresponds to a gene, strain and enzyme combination. For each category, the number of cases with regulatory hypomethylation in the window centred on the neighbouring transposase was compared with the number in the window centred on the gene itself, to test whether the pattern observed for resistance genes holds across adaptive functions.

```{r categorias interes}
# Define the 4 "adaptive" categories of interest for this analysis

categorias_interes <- c("Resistance", "Virulence/Adherence", "Toxin-Antitoxin/SOS", "Plasmid maintenance")
# Gene -> category dictionary, filtered to the categories of interest
dicc_cat <- vecindario_clasificado %>%
  filter(categoria %in% categorias_interes) %>%
  distinct(gen_vecino, categoria)

# Bridge cepa/locus_tag/gen_vecino, keeping "posicion" (upstream/downstream) 
puente_vecino <- tsv_raw %>%
  distinct(cepa, locus_tag, gen_vecino, posicion)
```

